posts.text:
Out of everything posted about FSD v15 so far, one line from @elonmusk deserves way more attention than it's getting: "This is real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator. Let that sink in …" 🔥

Half of one accelerator is the part worth sitting with. Once you see the numbers behind it, Reality View stops looking like a fancy new screen and starts looking like one of the most impressive things Tesla has ever shipped.

🎬 THE SCREEN IS NOW GENERATED LIVE

For years, FSD's screen worked like a video game. Software took a list of what the car detected and dropped stock 3D models in the right spots: a gray car here, a lane line there.

Reality View tosses that playbook out the window. The car's AI now generates the video itself, frame after frame, as you drive, with no game engine anywhere in the loop.

Better yet, the picture comes from the same end-to-end model that's doing the driving. That's the single neural network that turns camera video into steering and braking, and now it paints your screen, too.

⚙️ WHAT A TRIP ACTUALLY IS

The standard AI4 computer carries two self-driving chips, and each chip packs three custom neural processors Tesla calls TRIP accelerators. That's six in all.

And that's where Reality View gets made: right on the self-driving computer, instead of the infotainment chip that runs your maps and music.

Each TRIP is basically an arena packed with tiny calculators, all cranking through the multiply-and-add math that neural networks run on. Teardowns count 9,216 of them per TRIP, lined up in a 96-by-96 grid and firing 2.2 billion times a second.

Each calculator handles two operations per tick, so one TRIP works out to 9,216 × 2 × 2.2 billion, or roughly 40 trillion operations every second.

Half of one comes to about 20 trillion, roughly a twelfth of the whole computer's neural muscle.

📏 WHY THAT NUMBER IS RIDICULOUS

Twenty trillion operations per second sounds enormous, until you see what else runs on that kind of budget.

The Neural Engine inside Apple's iPhone 15 Pro is rated at 35 trillion operations per second. So on paper, the slice of compute painting Reality View has less raw AI muscle than the AI chip in a 2023 phone.

Companies don't all count these numbers the same way, so it's a ballpark, but it shows just how little compute this is.

At the other end of the scale sits Nvidia's H100, one of the data-center workhorses powering today's AI boom. It's rated at about 1,979 trillion 8-bit operations per second in its standard mode, the same kind of math a TRIP runs, which puts half a TRIP at roughly 1% of one H100.

That gap matters because AI video is one of the toughest jobs in AI. Many AI video generators still take minutes to produce a single clip, as the researchers behind the real-time system MotionStream point out.

Even MotionStream, built specifically for speed, streams roughly 17 to 29 frames per second at 480p, and about 10 at 720p, while eating up an entire H100.

Meanwhile, Tesla is streaming a live, photorealistic view of the real road on roughly 1% of that chip's rated power, inside a moving car.

In other words, Reality View runs on less compute than a phone's AI chip, inside a computer whose main job is driving.

There's a fair asterisk here. Those research models dream up whole scenes from a prompt or a single image, while Tesla's renderer starts with a driving brain that already knows exactly what's around the car. Tesla also hasn't shared the view's resolution or frame rate.

And even on the most generous estimates of AI4's power, half a TRIP still works out to only about 2% of one H100.

Either way, live generated video on a sliver of a car computer would have sounded like science fiction not long ago.

🔍 HOW IT CAN BE THIS CHEAP

Tesla hasn't spelled out how it works, but it has left plenty of breadcrumbs.

FSD's network has been building its own 3D picture of the world for a while now, something Tesla showed off at the ICCV conference in October 2025. That picture includes 3D Gaussians, millions of soft little blobs of color that can rebuild a scene you can view from any angle.

Tesla also built its own Gaussian splatting system that can rebuild a scene from the car's cameras in a fraction of a second.

Reality View streams its picture from a virtual camera that can sit anywhere above the car, and showing a scene from an angle no real camera has is exactly what those 3D blobs are great at.

Even Elon seems to like that theory: he called a description of Reality View as a neural, Gaussian-splat digital twin "pretty accurate", and it lines up with every other clue.

If that's the trick, the hard part is done before the screen ever needs a picture. The driving brain understands the scene, and the visualization just paints what it already knows.

That would explain the other shocker. Reality View swapped every separate signal behind the old screen for one end-to-end visualization, and it still uses less compute than the bare-bones 2020 visualization did.

🚗 WHY TESLA CARES SO MUCH

v15 is Tesla's large model, built to squeeze every ounce of performance out of HW4. On a chip working that hard, a screen that costs half of one TRIP leaves nearly everything else for the driving.

And it's a flex, too. The AI4 computer costs about $650 by Elon's own figure, and that same box now drives the car and paints live video of the world at the same time.

This is only the start. Elon says Tesla vehicles will share traffic knowledge and combine it with Grok's real-time 𝕏 feed, even giving you a heads-up about what's happening at your destination.

A view this cheap to generate is the perfect canvas for that kind of shared knowledge.

Elon asked everyone to let that sink in, and the math earns it: half of one accelerator in a $650 computer is painting the real world live while FSD drives.

• LoRa connects water-level sensors and the automated water gate

• Solar panels power the equipment where grid electricity is difficult to access

• Cloud monitoring gives operators real-time water levels, camera feeds, equipment status, and emergency alerts

• Workers remotely open and close the water gate without physically visiting the site

The results are already impressive:

All 6 remote gate-control tests were SUCCESSFUL

Workers now have visibility and control over infrastructure that previously required a dangerous mountain trip just to inspect

This becomes especially important during floods and emergencies, when every minute matters and sending workers into dangerous conditions puts lives at risk

Elon Musk explains why SpaceX catching Starship achieves the "holy grail of rocketry," and can cut the cost of access to space by 100x:

In 2025, SpaceX launched 2,200 tons to orbit, more than 80% of the global total.

Elon Musk's goal with Starship is 1,000,000 tons to orbit per year, about 450x what SpaceX launched last year.

Falcon 9 reuses its booster but throws away the upper stage on every flight. Starship is designed to bring back both.

"We've had three booster catches, but this is the first ship catch, which means we've now at least proven that all parts of Starship can be flown to space and recovered in good enough shape to be reflown."

"No one has ever taken a stage like that and created a truly reusable upper stage, and certainly not brought it back and had it land propulsively while being caught by giant chopsticks, which sounds like some kind of preposterous sci-fi book or something. But it's done."

"Starship can drop the cost of access to space by a factor of 100... and achieve a mass to orbit rate that is in the million ton per year range."

"This has been the holy grail of rocketry from the beginning, to have a fully reusable rocket system."

"The Space Shuttle was partially reusable, but the main tank… was thrown away on every flight… The shuttle orbiter, the plane-like thing, would take something like nine months to refurbish between flights."

"Whereas Starship is designed for complete reusability and to be reused immediately like an airplane. The booster lands, you can put another ship on top and take off immediately."

"The net effect of this, to put it into economic terms, is a hundredfold reduction in the cost of access to space, and maybe even eventually a thousandfold reduction."

"That's what's necessary in order to make life multiplanetary, in order to build a city on the Moon or Mars… You couldn't do it even if you had the whole budget of the United States government."

Elon Musk and SpaceX have been working toward a fully reusable orbital rocket for more than two decades.

Five days ago, they proved every part of Starship can fly to space and be recovered.

posts.text: We appreciate the SpaceX recovery teams for being immediately onsite following the Super Heavy booster's splashdown off the coast of Starbase, and for keeping our community informed.

ref.name: SpaceX
ref.text:
On Starship’s 15th flight last week, the Super Heavy booster correctly performed a safe abort when returning for a catch and ended its mission with a splashdown in the water off the coast of Starbase. Following splashdown, SpaceX recovery teams were immediately onsite to safe the area while our Environmental Health and Safety team worked to ensure any debris that washes onshore was recovered → http://x.com/SpaceX/status/2121629958036492590

When we received reports of potential debris in Mexican territory, we immediately mobilized to send specialists to aid in identification and lead any cleanup work required, just as we did on Boca Chica Beach near Starbase. We continue to stay in contact with the Mexican government and are on standby to send support if authorities in Mexico tell us it is actually needed. Partners on the ground relayed that theyhave found very little debris in their sweeps of the beach, and the small amount they have found are not clearly from SpaceX operations.

The majority of the social media posts online claiming widespread debris and damage are either outright fabrications or intentionally misleading. As repeatedly stated, independent tests conducted on materials inside Starship and the Super Heavy booster, including toxicity analyses, confirm they pose no chemical, biological, or toxicological risks.

Starship is designed to be fully reusable, with future missions planning to return all hardware back to the launch site for catch and reuse. SpaceX is the only one, whether company or country, that has demonstrated this capability is now possible.

Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls. Here are the 11 key takeaways:

1. SpaceX is scaling AI compute at an extraordinary pace:

SpaceX is adding roughly 500 MW monthly, equivalent to 220,000 GB300s. Elon expects over 1 GW monthly by end-2027: a 6 GW annualized pace today, doubling to 12 GW.

2. Its build costs are far below industry estimates:

Elon says outside estimates are off by up to 2x, with SpaceX building at roughly 60% of industry costs. Its in-house "Army X" builds the data centers, while Tesla Megapacks smooth training power. I'd already been modeling a 25–30% SpaceX cost advantage.

3. Anthropic could become a 10 GW customer:

Anthropic told Elon its most likely outcome is renting another 10 GW from SpaceX, on top of existing capacity. Contracts allow termination with 3–6 months' notice, but Anthropic says staying is "extremely likely." This reinforces my model that Anthropic will take most upcoming capacity.

4. SpaceX is targeting a vastly larger telecom market:

Elon argues AT&T and Verizon won't disappear as bandwidth demand explodes. Humans communicate at roughly 100 bits per second, while superintelligence and robots could require a trillion. SpaceX is targeting a market orders of magnitude larger than existing telecom revenue, as I'd modeled. Even more interestingly, this creates an opportunity to push its AI business further.

5. Its next-generation satellite network arrives next year:

Direct to Cell V2 launches with 40x V1's bandwidth. Micro cell towers using 800 MHz and rooftop units resembling Starlink dishes will extend indoor coverage, with rooftop hardware entering production next year. Starlink is becoming a full scale carrier.

6. SpaceXSI has rebuilt its entire AI software stack:

Over six to eight months, it rewrote training, reinforcement learning, and inference from scratch, close to the metal in C and C++. Elon thinks it "might have the best training stack software in the world." Grok 4.8 is also being built for practical usefulness rather than benchmark leadership, which is great for Grokbot.

7. Terafab could become the largest project on Earth:

The facility is planned to reach 100 million square feet, with phase-one volume production targeted for late 2028. Elon says established chipmakers are risk-averse because of massive capex, while SpaceX will take risks and iterate rapidly toward a better chip process by 2028.

8. Optimus is moving toward industrial work:

Elon expects an unstaged demonstration in a month or two and says Optimus could do dishes within 12–18 months. Its first major industrial role will be mining and refining ore for national security.

9. A Tesla–SpaceX merger is becoming increasingly logical:

Elon says the companies are "probably" better together as AI and robotics bring them closer. Both have AI software teams and advanced chip-design capabilities, while superintelligence compute could eventually move into orbit. Shareholders will decide; Elon says he shouldn't receive an award simply for merging them.

10. Ship 42 could accelerate the entire Starship reuse program:

Ship 42 needed only minor repairs before flying again, but SpaceX is retiring it for public display. This brings rapid reuse much closer.

11. SpaceX is targeting 200 GW of annual solar manufacturing for space:

That's roughly 40% of average US electricity consumption. Its Starmind compute unit delivers the same capability at roughly a quarter the size of a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, which is a win in space. Elon says it's also simpler than Starlink V3, which is already in production.

Simply put, SpaceX is building toward a trillion-dollar annual revenue business within just a few years, at scale never seen before.

Many of these numbers I've already modeled and shared over the past few months. Yesterday's announcements bring those projections closer to reality.

The scale of what's coming is extraordinary!

Elon Musk and Grimes found each other because they both independently made the same obscure joke about an AI thought experiment called Roko's Basilisk. Neither of them knew the other had made it. When they discovered the coincidence, Elon DM'd her. Their first real conversation lasted four hours.

Roko's Basilisk is a philosophical thought experiment about a future AI that punishes anyone who didn't help create it. It's the kind of idea that maybe a few thousand people on Earth find interesting, let alone funny. Elon had tweeted a joke about it. Grimes had made a music video referencing it. Neither one was aware of the other's version.

When someone pointed out the overlap, Elon messaged her. The conversation that followed wasn't flirting. It was two people discovering that their brains worked in the same strange way. AI, simulation theory, the future of consciousness, music as mathematics. Grimes later said she had never met anyone who could follow her thoughts at the speed she was thinking them.

Their first public appearance together was the 2018 Met Gala. They arrived together and the internet lost its mind because nobody could figure out how the richest man in tech and an experimental musician from Montreal ended up in the same universe.

The answer was simpler than anyone expected. They were both the kind of person who makes jokes about obscure AI philosophy at 2am and thinks that's normal. They didn't find each other through fame or fortune. They found each other through a thought experiment that maybe a thousand other people on Earth would have understood.

The rarest kind of connection isn't physical attraction. It's finding someone whose mind works like yours in a world that doesn't understand either of you.

BREAKING: SpaceXSI cuts invoicing time from 24 hours to minutes with Grok Bot.

Five specialized Grok Bots are now handling entire accounting jobs at SpaceXSI, with people stepping in for decisions and approvals:

• Customer accounts: Checks signed contracts, sets up customer access and removes access after contracts end.

• Billing: Checks contract details, catches errors and sends invoices—reducing the process from roughly 24 hours to minutes.

• Billing support: Answers questions and updates billing records. SpaceXSI estimates this bot alone saves its accounting team around 8 hours of work a day.

• Payments: Matches incoming payments to invoices and investigates differences. Work that normally takes an accountant 3–4 hours now takes roughly 30 minutes.

• Customer inquiries: Answers customer billing questions and coordinates requests such as refunds, which still require human approval.

SpaceXSI estimates that handling this workload without Grok Bot would require more than doubling its accounting team. Its accountants can now focus on improving systems and resolving complex issues.

SpaceXSI is showing how powerful Grok Bot can be for businesses: faster work, less time spent on routine tasks and more time for people to focus on what needs their expertise.
